answer: A random 11% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. Because the grove sample is drawn from the cipher beacon, the beacon audit shows the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is published per key. A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. That is 20 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
